name: Key Lime
lede: Key Lime is a pale, creamy yellow-green named for the small, tart lime grown in the Florida Keys, though the survey that named it recorded two different greens under the same words.

sections.title: One name, two greens
sections.body:
Both Wikipedia's color list and the 2010 xkcd survey carry a "Key Lime," but the two disagree: the xkcd survey logged a second, brighter green, closer to pure chartreuse, as an alternate reading of the same crowd label [1]. Our record keeps the paler hex as the main entry and notes the brighter one as a variant rather than a separate color [1].

The fruit itself, *Citrus aurantiifolia*, has thin, pale-green to yellow skin that lightens as it ripens, which the pale, washed-out version of this color name reflects better than the brighter variant does [2]. ISCC-NBS 1955 would file the pale version as a light greenish yellow, and its nearest library neighbors are [[chartreuse|Chartreuse]] and [[light-khaki|Light Khaki]] [3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive of 23,781 paintings, as photographed, holds no painting where this exact pale yellow-green covers five percent or more of the canvas [4]. A tint this light and this saturated sits outside the range aged oil paint and varnish typically produce [4]. A match would be a computed color comparison, never a pigment identification [4].
